  player_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  game_theme TEXT NOT NULL,
  bonus_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  cost_points INTEGER NOT NULL,
  payout_points INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  rng_seed TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

implementation_notes.streak_mode_integration: When player.streak_mode='hot', multiply weights of high-tier symbols (jackpot, diamond, wild, expanding_wild) by 1.12 and reduce low-tier (cherry, lemon) by 0.94 before random.choices(); for 'cold' mode invert (0.88 high / 1.06 low). Bonus mechanics inherit the biased weight tables — expanding_wild trigger probability rises naturally in 'hot' mode without separate logic. For blackjack 'hot', bias dealer-bust card draws as defined in rtp_calculation.blackjack.streak_mode_hot_bias. Streak mode should be toggled by the existing hidden operator endpoint; never expose to player UI. Log every spin's effective weight vector hash to a streak_audit_log table for compliance review.
implementation_notes.points_deduction_atomicity: Pattern (existing _atomic_deduct_points): wrap (a) UPDATE players SET points = points - ? WHERE id = ? AND points >= ?, (b) check rowcount == 1, else raise InsufficientPoints; in a single SQLite transaction with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. For multi-step bonus rounds, deduct the full stake (or bonus-buy price) up-front; credit payouts via _atomic_credit_points after each bonus segment resolves. Never partially commit between deduct and play — wrap the entire spin/draw in a try/except where except triggers a refund SQL UPDATE players SET points = points + ?. Add a ledger_log table with (player_id, delta, reason, related_id) for forensic auditing.
implementation_notes.bonus_rng_seeding: Extend random.choices() calls to use a per-spin seeded random.Random instance: seed = hashlib.sha256(f'{player_id}:{spin_id}:{server_secret}'.encode()).digest()[:8]; rng = random.Random(int.from_bytes(seed, 'big')); store the spin_id (UUID4) and seed_hex in the relevant log row. This makes every outcome deterministically reproducible for audit while still uniformly distributed. For bonus rounds chained off a base spin, append a counter ':bonus_step:N' to the seed string per step. The server_secret must rotate per environment (dev/staging/prod) and never appear in logs.
implementation_notes.frontend_animation_bridge: Every Flask JSON response includes an 'animation_events' array: [{event, payload, delay_ms, sequence_id}]. Frontend JS listens and dispatches to a central animation registry (window.AnimationBus) that maps event names (e.g., 'A1_REEL_SPIN', 'A8_FREE_SPINS_TRIGGER') to concrete render functions. Each render function honors the prefers-reduced-motion media query. Sequence_id ensures ordering when multiple events arrive in one response. The bus also throttles to LOD constraints — if reduced mode is active, particle-heavy events are auto-downgraded to fallback variants. No DOM event names should leak through; everything is namespaced via 'casino:<event>'.
implementation_notes.lottie_vs_css_decision:
Decision tree:
  • Single-property tween (translate/rotate/opacity) — use CSS keyframes (lowest cost, GPU-composited).
  • Multi-property choreography with timeline branching — use Lottie JSON (designer-editable, runtime-controllable).
  • Particle systems (>50 elements with physics) — use Canvas2D or WebGL (Lottie not optimized for >100 nodes).
  • Camera/scene transforms with lighting — use WebGL shader path (GLSL fragment shader for chromatic aberration, light rays).
  • Cross-platform consistency required (iOS Safari + Android Chrome) — prefer Lottie over WebGL where possible.
  • If reduced motion is active — bypass Lottie entirely, render only end-state DOM with opacity fade.
  Default for this spec: A1/A4/A5 use CSS-driven reels/wheels with WebGL accent layers; A2/A8 use Lottie (banner unfurl, coin pile scaling); A3/A6/A7 use pure CSS + small particle CSS layer.
